pr_title: ReadOnlyByteBuf (and sub-classes) does not create derived buffers tha…
pr_body:
…t share reference count

Motivation:

The derived buffers that are created via ReadOnlyByteBuf (and sub-classes) do not share the reference count with the parent. This results in buffer leaks

Modifications:

- Correctly share reference count
- Add unit tests

Result:

Fix https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14075

issue_context.title: ByteBuf.asReadOnly() derived buffer doesn't support parent.release on deallocation which makes it unsuitable for ctx.write
issue_context.body:
### Expected behavior

It should be possible to share the reference count ownership to the read-only wrapper returned by `.asReadOnly()` in a similar way as `.duplicate()` behaves.

The behavior is well explained in a comment in AbstractPooledDerivedByteBuf:
https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/5085cef149134951c94a02a743ed70025c8cdad4/buffer/src/main/java/io/netty/buffer/AbstractPooledDerivedByteBuf.java#L32-L37

Without this support, it makes `.asReadOnly()` buffers unsuitable for use in writing to a channel pipeline where the reference count is decreased after the write completes. This would be needed for the use case explained in #14069 where it would be desired to write a shared ByteBuf instance to multiple clients that use TLS connections. One of the solution proposals would be to make the ByteBuf a read-only buffer so that SslHandler knows to avoid mutating the buffer.

### Actual behavior

The read-only wrapper doesn't call parent.release on deallocation. This makes it unsuitable for ctx.write calls where the reference count is decremented after the writing completes and this propagates to the parent buffer.

review_comments: The reason why read-only ByteBuffers are needed in the SslHandler use case is to avoid mutating the buffer. JDK's SSLEngine will mutate the input buffer with an in-place encryption reusing the input buffer unless the buffer is read-only. The support for read-only ByteBuffers in JDK's SSLEngine was added as a result of a bug reported by @chrisvest, more details in comment https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14069#issuecomment-2129279047 .
